title: Isandro and the Ghost
premise: Crash investigator Zephyrine Ashgrove has lived in hiding since the plane accident that killed her husband and daughter in row twelve—an accident she suspects was no accident, and for which she may be the only living witness. When a real-estate listing exposes the interior of her safe house, she realizes someone has been inside, photographing evidence of her survival, and that the same network is preparing a second 'accident' timed to a diplomatic summit. Racing a countdown she can barely prove, Zephyrine allies with a disgraced air-safety auditor who may be the only person who believes her, and discovers the crash was staged to cover a data-smuggling operation she unknowingly carried in her own investigation files. In the end she stops the summit attack by forcing the conspirators to trigger their failsafe early, exposing them publicly—but to do it she must surrender her invisibility, testify under her real name, and accept that belonging means being seen, even by those who want her dead.
about_author: Casper Joubert is the pen name of a former aviation-incident analyst who spent a decade writing confidential accident reports before turning to fiction. He lives quietly in a coastal town, still unable to sleep through the night.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Two years after the crash, she works nights investigating other people's accidents and sleeps in a locked room at dawn, haunted by a recording only she noticed. When she finds her safe house listed online with photos of her own kitchen, the emotional beat is dread turning to fury: someone has been inside.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine traces the listing to a brokerage that doesn't exist, and finds the photos include her case files—her secret evidence from the crash. POV shifts briefly to an unnamed watcher photographing a summit venue. The beat is the collapse of safety: invisibility was an illusion she paid for with her family's truth.

chapters.title: The Auditor
chapters.summary: Zephyrine approaches Elias Verhoeven, a disgraced auditor fired for claiming the crash was staged. Their wary first meeting in a rail-yard café crackles with distrust and recognition—two people exiled for telling the truth. Beat: the first fragile alliance, and the first admission she says his name out loud and it doesn't hurt.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Never Said
chapters.summary: Elias and Zephyrine reconstruct the flight data and discover the cockpit voice recording was overwritten with a loop—impossible without ground access. Her own archived files contain a smuggled data package she unknowingly carried. Beat: grief curdling into purpose; love beginning as intellectual partnership.

chapters.title: The Man from the Brokerage
chapters.summary: A polite stranger visits Zephyrine, offering her a settlement and a new identity in exchange for her original files. She records him; he leaves a threat against Elias. POV alternates with the watcher, who is revealed as a former colleague. Beat: the enemy becomes personal, and so does the choice between safety and loyalty.

chapters.title: Countdown to the Summit
chapters.summary: The pair decodes the smuggled data: flight-control firmware, weaponized, scheduled to fail a delegation's aircraft during the summit—another row-twelve-style accident. They have six days and no institution they can trust. Beat: rising dread, and a quiet scene where Zephyrine sleeps for the first time, in Elias's kitchen.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Their safe contact is murdered and staged as a suicide; the frame closes around Zephyrine herself, whose 'death' two years ago becomes evidence of fraud. Hunted, she realizes the conspirators need her files destroyed and her silence permanent. Beat: despair, then defiance—she decides to stop hiding and go to the summit.

chapters.title: Sixty Seconds of Static
chapters.summary: Infiltrating the summit's aviation liaison office, Zephyrine and Elias attempt to flag the compromised firmware, but the conspirators accelerate the plan. In a tense mid-flight intervention she forces the failsafe to trigger early, over open radio and dozens of witnesses, exposing the sabotage. Beat: the climax—love against duty as Elias must choose between protocol and her.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Zephyrine testifies under her real name, giving up the ghost of her hidden life, identifying the network that killed her family. The watcher, a colleague who once loved her, turns state's witness. Beat: catharsis through exposure; the cost of truth acknowledged without sentimentality.

chapters.title: Through the Night
chapters.summary: Months later, Zephyrine returns to the rebuilt crash site memorial with Elias, reads row twelve's names aloud, and sleeps through the night for the first time. The safe house is finally, truly for sale. Beat: resolution—belonging found not in invisibility but in being witnessed, and in choosing to stay.
